findings.title: Gait returns to a middle line
findings.claim: The measured-gait command takes up the proud, excessive walking of 31:18 and gives it a straight, moderated line. Movement remains the subject; the focus changes its public manner from display to proportion.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the command to direct one's own walk. The preceding ayah supplies swagger and joy beyond measure as independent context. Their contact lets straightness and a middle between extremes describe a corrected gait rather than an isolated etiquette rule.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear moderation as a way of restoring direction and scale to walking, rather than as a demand to shrink movement or ambition.
findings.containment: The plain instruction to walk with measure remains fully available. The context can also be read as a neighboring warning about conduct; the packet does not require every gait and voice instruction to form one metaphor.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence names the focus and context carriers, branch nominations, and changed reading; the supplied connection independently links the immediately preceding prohibition of proud walking to this command.

findings.claim: The acoustic comparison can also return to 31:17: commands to enjoin recognized good and restrain wrong, followed by patience, meet a focus superlative from the same NKR root. The voice used for correction can therefore be heard as subject to the very test of acceptability it applies.
findings.mechanism: The contextual carriers are the supplied directives to enjoin good and forbid wrong, together with patience. The focus returns through voice and the NKR superlative applied to sounds. Their repeated root and neighboring acts of restraint let the sound warning operate reflexively: the form of correction can itself become repellent or lose legibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The donkey comparison remains acoustic, while the reader can also hear a question about how correction sounds: restraint governs delivery as well as persistence.
findings.containment: This is an attributed, qualified pericope reading. The focus NKR can remain purely sonic and its echo with 31:17 lexical; the bundle does not prescribe a volume or adjudicate between these readings.

findings.title: Body and voice return to measured presence
findings.claim: The prior ayah gathers a turned cheek, exuberant gait, swagger, and boast into public self-display. The focus answers through the same walking channel and adds voice reduction, so bodily and audible presence can be read together as brought back to measure.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are measured gait, reduction, and voice; the independent 31:18 triggers are physical separation, excess joy, swagger, and boasting. Their contact across the ayah boundary links the body's displayed scale to sound and changes two adjacent manners into a coordinated correction of outward presence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the paired instructions as reducing a bid to dominate shared space, while retaining purposeful movement and audible speech.
findings.containment: The commands still mean measured walking and lower voice. The integration is an attributed contextual reading; the HFT record also leaves open treating gait and voice as separate manners, and neither account displaces the literal commands.
